question: Put these milestones in the founding of Gilead School in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 23

items: September 1942: directors approve N. H. Knorr's proposal for the school
December 14, 1942: invitations sent to prospective students
February 1, 1943: the first class opens
Five months later: the first class graduates and leaves for Latin America

question: Put these early Watch Tower missionary milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapters 23-24

items: 1910: William Johnston is sent to Nyasaland (now Malawi)
1923: W. R. Brown leaves for Africa
1942: the Gilead School proposal is approved
1947: Ted and Doris Klein arrive in the Virgin Islands

question: Put these events of Nazi-era persecution in Germany in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 24

items: The Nazis rise to power in Germany
Persecution of Jehovah's Witnesses intensifies under Nazi control
October 7, 1934: Hitler declares the group will be exterminated
June 24, 1936: a special Gestapo Command is formed to fight the Witnesses

question: Put these events, showing how Witnesses ended up preaching within the Soviet Union, in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 24

items: During the 1920s-1930s, Soviet officials deny permission to ship in or print Bible literature
World War II ends, and Polish Witnesses find themselves within Soviet borders due to border changes
In the Ravensbrück concentration camp, Russian women prisoners come to know fellow Witness prisoners
The released Russian women return to various parts of the Soviet Union

question: Put these early Russell-era publishing milestones in order.

items: 1877: the pamphlet The Object and Manner of Our Lord's Return is published
1879: Zion's Watch Tower and Herald of Christ's Presence begins publication
1881: the first call for colporteur evangelists goes out
1903: the Watch Tower recommends house-to-house tract distribution

question: Put these mass-media milestones in the preaching work in order.

1922: J. F. Rutherford makes his first radio broadcast
1924: radio station WBBR begins broadcasting
1933: radio broadcasting of the Kingdom message peaks at 408 stations

question: Put these doorstep preaching technologies in the order they were introduced.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 25

items: 1933: testimony cards are introduced
1934: portable phonographs are carried in cars for witnessing
1937: the phonograph is used right on the doorstep
1940: more than 40,000 phonographs are in use

question: Put these public-witnessing milestones in order.

question: Put these home-Bible-study aids and milestones in order.

items: 1921: the book The Harp of God is published for beginners
1936: the book Riches is used to establish home Bible studies

question: Put these early Russell-era publishing beginnings in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1876: Russell's first article appears in the Bible Examiner
1877: Russell funds the book Three Worlds with N. H. Barbour
1879: Russell begins Zion's Watch Tower after breaking with Barbour
February 16, 1881: the Zion's Watch Tower Tract Society is formed

question: Put these Society incorporation and naming milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1881: the Tract Society is formed with W. H. Conley as president
1884: the Society is legally incorporated with Russell as president
1896: the name changes to Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society
1898: Russell donates the Tower Publishing Company's assets to the Society

question: Put these Millennial Dawn / Studies in the Scriptures publishing milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1886: Russell completes writing The Divine Plan of the Ages
1886-1897: the first four volumes are published
By 1916: over 9,384,000 of the six volumes have been distributed
1917: the seventh volume, The Finished Mystery, is released

question: Put these 1918-1919 disruption-and-rebuilding events in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1918: the Brooklyn headquarters is dismantled and its printing plates destroyed
The greatly reduced staff moves the office back to Pittsburgh
1919: the Cedar Point convention announces the new magazine The Golden Age
October 1919: operations resume in Brooklyn after the "coal test"

question: Put these steps of the "coal test" story in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: Rutherford tells C. A. Wise to test whether returning to Brooklyn is the Lord's will
Rutherford recommends making coal the test and ordering 500 tons
Wise applies to the authorities and is granted a certificate for 500 tons of coal
By October 1, 1919, operations resume in Brooklyn

question: Put these steps in setting up the Society's own printing operations in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: Early 1920: the Society leases floors at 35 Myrtle Avenue for its first printing shop
February 1, 1920: an issue of The Watch Tower is printed on the Society's own press for the first time
1921: the Society considers whether to also print and bind its own books
March 1, 1922: brothers move into 18 Concord Street to print and bind their own books

question: Put these world headquarters factory expansion milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1926: the Society purchases land in Brooklyn for its own factory
February 1927: the Society moves into its new building at 117 Adams Street
Within ten years: the factory has to be enlarged
1942: complete Bibles begin to be printed there

question: Put these post-World War II printing expansion milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1946: Knorr announces expansion plans at an international assembly in Cleveland
Early 1950: the enlarged factory and Bethel Home are completed
1969: work begins designing a new printery near Wallkill, New York
By 1977: the Wallkill presses turn out 18 million magazines a month

question: Put these offset-printing transition milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1972: the South Africa Bethel family buys a small secondhand offset press
1974: that press prints a pocket-size book in the Ronga language
1975: Germany uses a sheetfed offset press for East German literature
1978: the first web offset press for books begins operating in Brooklyn

question: Put these MEPS computer development milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: 1977: the decision is made to develop a computerized prepress system
1979: the MEPS project begins at Watchtower Farms, Wallkill
By May 1986: MEPS software supports 186 languages
By 1992: over 3,800 terminals worldwide use the Society's own software

question: Put these global printing decentralization milestones in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26

items: Late 1960s: a concerted decentralization effort begins
1969: work begins on designing the Wallkill printery
1971: work begins on a new printing plant in Numazu, Japan
By the end of 1975: the Society publishes literature in its own facilities in 23 lands

question: Put these typesetting technologies used by the Society in the order they came into use.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26, p. 581

items: At first, typesetting is done by hand, one letter at a time
From 1920, Linotype machines are used
In some places, Monotype equipment is used
Now, a computerized phototypesetting process is used

question: Put these steps of letterpress platemaking in order.
reference: Jehovah's Witnesses—Proclaimers of God's Kingdom, Chapter 26, p. 582

items: Lines of type are locked into metal frames called chases
Under pressure, an impression of the type is made on a mold material
Hot lead is poured against the mold to make curved metal printing plates
The plates are nickeled for durability

Sewing them together
